title: The Turtle Ship Before Dawn
synopsis: The gunpowder for the turtle ship is gone from the store room.
A note with a small water drop is waiting on the empty shelf.
goal: Find out who moved the gunpowder, and where, before dawn.

notes: Played as a search (InvestigationScene): Ham's three report lines say where each thing is (under, next to, on). The question asks which find shows that rain came in over the powder: the Admiral's words say wet powder will not fire, and the bucket is full of rain under the roof hole. The options are listed straw, note, bucket (never answer first). Ham's count (twelve) is not said before M3.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of store_room.webp (picture.measuredOn): the roof hole upper left of centre with its wet patch below (the bucket placed there), the long empty shelf across the back, the door on the right with the straw at its foot, the rope shelves on the left; no two areas overlap.
The note is drawn as a blank folded paper with a small blue water drop: no writing in any picture.

notes: The rain blurred the note's lines and dots; what is left names each group's sounds by the part of the mouth on the sailors' letter board, which the mission shows, and its vowel by the dot and line. The groups sit one under another, top to bottom (one column). The note reads 거북선, the turtle ship.
Two first sounds are not used (ㅁ, ㅈ): 'the lips + 1 line' is ㅂ, not ㅁ; 'the teeth' is ㅅ, not ㅈ.
Every letter is the app's text (SyllableBoard): never in a picture.

The sailors' letter board hangs on the store room wall; Ham reads only Chinese letters, so the board, not Ham, teaches the King's letters. Rookie says '+ 1 line'; Junior and Master say 'one more line' or 'one step stronger'.

learning.objective: 창고 벽 수병 글자판(입 모양을 본뜬 자음, a stronger sound adds one line)과 위치 표현(a dot on its left, under it, at the bottom)을 읽고 번진 쪽지의 세 글자를 세로로 다시 만든다.
expressions: a standing line, with a dot on its left

play.title: The Blurred Note
story: You hold the wet note under Ham's lamp.
Three groups of letters, one under another. The rain blurred their lines and dots.
"I cannot read the King's letters," says Ham. "I read only Chinese letters."
"But the young sailors learn them from that board on the wall."
play.letterIntro: The board on the store room wall:
play.letter:
THE SAILORS' LETTER BOARD
The King's letters copy the mouth:
ㄱ = the back of the tongue
ㄴ = the tongue
ㅁ = the lips
ㅅ = the teeth
A stronger sound adds one line.
ㄴ + 1 line = ㄷ
ㅁ + 1 line = ㅂ
A flat line goes under the first sound.
A standing line goes on its right.
A sound at the bottom comes last.
play.question: Build the three groups, from top to bottom. What does the note say?
hints: Group 1 is at the top. Find the back of the tongue on the board.
The lips + 1 line is ㅂ. Choose each sound, then its line and dot.
play.successMessage: The note is whole again: 거북선, the turtle ship!
transition: Someone carried the powder to the turtle ship!
You and Ham hurry down to the harbour.

feedback.거묵선: Group 2 is the lips + 1 line: ㅂ, not ㅁ.
feedback.거북서: Group 3 has a sound at the bottom: the tongue.
feedback.가북선: Group 1's dot is on the left of its line, not the right.
feedback.거북전: Group 3 is the teeth, not the teeth + 1 line.

play.title: Under the Turtle's Back
story: The turtle ship has a roof of planks over its deck.

A young sailor stands up, his clothes wet. "I am Seok. I carried them here."

"I took four barrels each time, in a hand cart."
"I went from the store room to the ship three times."
"The ship's roof keeps the rain off."

transition: Ham opens his book from sunset: twelve barrels.
"All twelve are here," Ham says. "But he moved them with no order!"
The sky turns grey. The Admiral is coming aboard.

intro: Spring, 1592: the fourth month of the moon calendar.
You are a guest of Admiral Yi Sun-sin at Yeosu, on the south coast.
He commands the navy here. War with Japan may come soon.
Before the war, he built a turtle ship, with a roof over its deck.
"Today we test its cannons," he says. "We must be ready."
Before dawn, a bell rings at the store room.
play.caseSummary: Rain came through the store room roof. Seok, a young sailor, carried all twelve barrels of gunpowder to the turtle ship. He left a note in the King's letters, with a water drop for the rain. The detective showed the Admiral that nothing was stolen. Yi Sun-sin had built the turtle ship before the war. Its front was a dragon's head. On the twelfth day of the fourth month of 1592, its cannons were tested. His war diary records it. The next day, Japanese ships came to Busan, and the war began. In the fifth month, his navy won its first victory at sea, at Okpo.

notes: PART 10 (2026-11-06), Case 02. Admiral Yi Sun-sin is real; his words here are made up (two lines of the final retell the 1592 record of the turtle ship, s5_ep02_h1). Seok and Quartermaster Ham are made up; so are the store room, the rain and the night's test.

Ends on checked facts: the final asks what really happened to the powder, judged with this case's three cards (rain through the store room roof, the note naming the turtle ship, twelve dry barrels); the transition names the real dragon head with a cannon hole (h1). The ending tells the real cannon test of the 12th day of the 4th lunar month, 1592, in Yi's diary (h5), the war's start at Busan the next day (h3, lunar 13th), the first victory at sea at Okpo in the 5th lunar month (h4), and the King's wish that the letters be easy to learn (h11). All dates are of the lunar calendar; no solar date is given.
